answer: Coordination Ledge Pricing. Each agent must post a per-action fee on an onyx ledger that scales with its recent unique-counterparty count; fees accrue to the counterparties, not the protocol. New identities start on a low walnut-tier limit, capping how many distinct peers they can touch per epoch. An attacker must fund a fresh fee balance for every sybil and absorb the full cost of each synthetic interaction, making N fake agents cost roughly N times the honest per-peer rate.
